ablauf.27: Ein Auto beschleunigt aus der Ruhe gleichmäßig in 8,0 s auf 24 m/s. Welche Strecke legt es dabei zurück?
ablauf.30: The car gets faster by the same amount every second: uniformly accelerated motion. Imagine it drove the whole time at a fixed average speed; it would get just as far. This picture only holds as long as the acceleration stays constant.
ablauf.32: v equals v zero plus a times t
ablauf.33: s equals v zero times t plus one half a t squared
ablauf.34: Why may you use the average of the initial and final velocity here?
ablauf.35: No solution. Work it out yourself, about 10 minutes; otherwise tipp.
ablauf.36: Which quantity is wanted, and which three values do you know?
ablauf.37: What does “from rest” mean for the initial velocity?
ablauf.38: Why may you assume constant acceleration here?
ablauf.39: Which law links velocity, acceleration and time?
ablauf.40: How do you get from the acceleration to the distance?
ablauf.41: How can you tell whether your distance is plausible?
ablauf.42: The solution is held back. Answer the questions on paper, 10 minutes at most.
ablauf.44: A train travels at 72 km/h and brakes uniformly to a stop in 16.0 s. How long is the braking distance?
ablauf.45: v zero equals 72 kilometres per hour equals 20 metres per second
ablauf.46: a equals minus 1.25 metres per second squared
ablauf.47: s equals v zero t plus one half a t squared
ablauf.48: s equals 20 metres per second times 16.0 seconds minus one half times 1.25 metres per second squared times 16.0 seconds squared
ablauf.49: s equals 320 metres minus 160 metres equals 160 metres
ablauf.51: Average speed 10 m/s times 16.0 s also gives 160 m.
ablauf.52: Your turn: the car problem with the same method, about 10 minutes. To compare: kurz.
ablauf.54: a equals 24 metres per second divided by 8.0 seconds equals 3.0 metres per second squared
ablauf.55: with v zero equal to zero: s equals one half a t squared
ablauf.56: s equals one half times 3.0 metres per second squared times 8.0 seconds squared equals 96 metres
ablauf.58: “From rest” means v₀ = 0; that is why the term v₀t drops out.

forschung.01: Built on 23 studies from learning research.
forschung.02: The tutor’s teaching rules follow principles backed by experiments and seven meta-analyses. Every study is evaluated openly in the repository.
forschung.04: That is how much Harvard students in introductory physics learned with an AI tutor built on learning principles: more than twice as much as in active in-person teaching, in 49 instead of 60 minutes. They also felt more engaged and motivated.
forschung.05: What matters is how it is built: with free AI access, around 1,000 learners did worse in a later test without help; with an AI tutor that had safeguards, they did not (Bastani et al. 2025, PNAS).
forschung.06: The tutor does both: it guides you step by step and gives the solution only on request.
forschung.08: How strongly the principles work, according to meta-analyses
forschung.10: Wisniewski, Zierer & Hattie 2020 · subgroup of a meta-analysis of 435 studies
forschung.15: Effect size compared with control groups; 0.5 counts as a medium effect.
forschung.17: Recall it yourself instead of rereading
forschung.18: Actively retrieving what you learned keeps it better after days than reading it again.
forschung.20: In the tutor: explanations end with a Verständnisfrage (comprehension question); the answer comes only on request.
forschung.22: Put the why into your own words
forschung.23: Prompts to justify steps yourself clearly improve learning on average (g = 0.55), especially when they ask about concepts.
forschung.24: Chi et al. 1989, 1994 · Bisra et al. 2018
forschung.25: In the tutor: tipp asks guiding questions, at least one about the why.
forschung.27: Worked through, but not your problem
forschung.28: Fully worked examples improve maths performance (g = 0.43). They help beginners most; advanced learners need fewer of them.
forschung.29: Sweller & Cooper 1985 · Kalyuga et al. 2003 · Barbieri et al. 2023
forschung.30: In the tutor: voll works through a different problem.
forschung.33: Feedback with information works much better than praise or a bare right/wrong.
forschung.35: In the tutor: check names the first mistake with the reason.
forschung.37: AI as a supplement, not a replacement
forschung.38: People who get explanations from AI understand a topic better than people who let it produce the solution.
forschung.39: Lehmann et al. 2024/25 · Bastani et al. 2025
forschung.40: In the tutor: help in steps from erklär to kurz.
forschung.43: The best gap between study sessions depends on how long you want to remember.
forschung.44: Cepeda et al. 2006, 2008 · Dunlosky et al. 2013
forschung.45: In the tutor: the review card plans “in 2–3 days and again after about a week”.
forschung.46: The studies support the learning principles the tutor is built on. All sources with study design and assessment (in German):learning research review and evidence update.

fragen.02: What kinds of problems is the tutor made for?
fragen.03: For exercise and exam problems in physics, maths, electrical engineering and engineering mechanics at university. You send a photo or the text of the problem, optionally with a command word like tipp.
fragen.05: Nothing. The tutor is free, ad-free and open source (MIT licence). You only need a Claude account; according to the Claude help, skills are available on all plans, including the free one.
fragen.06: Can I learn on my phone?
fragen.07: Yes: you upload the skill once in the browser on claude.ai. After that you photograph problems in your phone’s browser and send them straight away. The Claude app has not been fully tested for this yet.
fragen.09: Yes, with a course pack: a Markdown file with the notation and syllabus of your course, e.g. kurse/mpg1.md. Upload it as project knowledge in a Claude project and study in that project.
fragen.11: It is designed for it: short sections, always the same order and, at the end, exactly one next step with a time estimate.
fragen.13: Replies are more consistent: “Gegeben / Gesucht” is always a table, numbers use Latin digits in Arabic and Persian too, and in erklär the solutions come at the very end. Since v0.3.0-rc.4, explanations are available in Persian instead of Urdu ([fa]). Carried over from v0.3.0-rc.3: erklär, voll and thema now explain along a fixed arc: an opening, one picture, its limit, a core sentence and the bridge to the equation. tipp asks about the why and offers a different approach if you write “weiß nicht” (don’t know). The review card plans two dates, formula symbols appear in the form that suits the platform, and there are subject rules for electrical engineering, engineering mechanics and maths. Everything in the changelog.
fragen.14: The tutor does not behave as described.
fragen.15: Check that “Code execution and file creation” is on and that the skill “tutor” is active under Customize → Skills. Then open a new chat and type only tutor. If no command card appears, delete the skill and upload the ZIP file again.
fragen.17: Upload the ZIP file unchanged. Unzipping and re-zipping it often loses the folder tutor/ at the top level; then Claude does not recognise the skill.
fragen.18: Formulas show up with dollar signs.
fragen.19: On claude.ai in the browser, formulas are rendered. If you see dollar signs, the platform does not display LaTeX; that is why the tutor writes formula symbols for ChatGPT in italics with subscripts (v₀).
fragen.20: How do I get a new version?
fragen.21: Download the new ZIP file, delete the old skill under Customize → Skills via “…” and upload the new file.
